description:
FILED s465 (Fable, 2026-09-03) from the BB (#994) merge review.

BB's finding: the standing tools/bench-exec.pl rows are BLIND to the tail-return transform -- `fib` ends in an IMPLICIT tail expression and `gcdrec`'s returns carry statement modifiers -- so the ~30 % win on an explicit-tail `return` (fibret 0.698 s -> 0.478 s) was invisible to every row the tool has.  BB added four rows in its scratch instrument (scratchpad p994/scratch-bb/wallab.pl and bench-section.pl: fibret, gcdret, subret, methret) that are not in the tree.

WHAT TO DO: add the explicit-`return` spellings to tools/bench-exec.pl as standing rows beside their implicit-tail twins (fib/fibret, gcd/gcdret, a plain sub-call row and a method-call row), so a return-protocol change (#964, #994, #77, the #1035 p-let printer) is measured by the bench and not by a one-off.  Record the K=5 control spread the tool reads on each row (round-23 measured Â±6.2 % for the pair).  A row is a measurement, not a target: do not tune the runtime for the row.

RELATED: #994 (DONE section has the numbers), #996 (the catalogue items never taken), #995 (measured, waiting), docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md.


=== DONE (s469bh) ===

Four rows added to tools/bench-exec.pl beside their implicit-tail twins, each
verified to contain exactly ONE `p-tail-value` in its emission and each
passing the tool's own BROKEN check (both engines' stdout equal at N_big):

  fibret    30 x fib(27), the sub ending in a plain tail `return TERNARY`
  gcdret    100k gcds, `my ($x,$y)=@_` params, the RECURSION as the tail return
  subret    3M calls of a plain non-recursive sub ending in `return $x + 1`
  methret   1M method calls ending in `return $self->{v} + 1`

gcdret's SHAPE WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, not taste.  The obvious spelling --
two `if (...) { return gcd... }` blocks and a trailing `return $x` -- leaves
the recursive returns NON-tail (only the sub body's LAST statement reaches the
transform), and the row then reads -0.0 % under PCL_OPT=-tail-return: it
measures the transform not firing.  The base case is the guarded block
instead, so the tail return is the exit taken on every recursive step.
gcdrec stays as the twin that reaches the transform not at all.

MEASURED on a QUIET box (best-of-5).  Run-to-run control spread on the pcl
column across two runs of the same tree: <= 1.1 % (max on gcdret).  The
byte-identical perl column between the ON and OFF runs below agreed to within
1.0 / 5.9 / 1.7 / 1.1 %, which is the control for the A/B:

  bench     perl(s)  pcl ON   pcl OFF   OFF vs ON   pcl/perl ON -> OFF
  fibret     1.51    0.4473   0.6242     +39.6 %     0.30x -> 0.42x
  gcdret     0.20    0.0924   0.1068     +15.6 %     0.47x -> 0.51x
  subret     0.21    0.0865   0.1187     +37.2 %     0.41x -> 0.56x
  methret    0.09    0.1436   0.1563      +8.8 %     1.58x -> 1.74x

(OFF = PCL_OPT=-tail-return, which the transpile picks up from the
environment.)  So the four rows DO see the transform, which is the whole
point of the task: methret's smaller move against subret's is the contrast
worth keeping -- it says how much of a dispatch-heavy program the return
protocol can be.

The full-table numbers with the twins, same quiet window:

  fib(27)x   1.4398 / 0.4179  0.29x      gcdrec  0.1882 / 0.0991  0.53x
  fibret     1.4576 / 0.4477  0.31x      gcdret  0.1899 / 0.0884  0.47x
  subret     0.2122 / 0.0860  0.41x      methret 0.0918 / 0.1360  1.48x

A row is a measurement, not a target: nothing was tuned for one.

Commit: e57a7e2 (tools/bench-exec.pl only; no emission change, no generation
bump).
subject: BENCH GAP: tools/bench-exec.pl has no EXPLICIT-`return` rows (fib ends in an implicit tail, gcdrec's returns carry modifiers), so the return protocol's cost is invisible to the standing bench -- add fibret / gcdret / subret / methret beside their implicit twins (BB's scratch wallab.pl has them)
